001package com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.response.historyLog;
002
003import org.apache.commons.lang3.Validate;
004import com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.annotations.HistoryLogProps;
005import com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.annotations.MessageProps;
006import com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.helpers.Bytes;
007import com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.helpers.Dates;
008import com.jwoglom.pumpx2.shared.JavaHelpers;
009
010import java.time.Instant;
011import java.util.Arrays;
012import java.util.HashSet;
013import java.util.Set;
014
015public abstract class HistoryLog {
016    /**
017     * Tolerance, in units of insulin, for comparing the float insulin amounts reported across
018     * history logs.
019     *
020     * <p>Values which are arithmetically equal can differ by one unit in the last place across
021     * logs, so consumers reconciling or deduplicating boluses should compare within this tolerance
022     * rather than testing float equality. The observation motivating this (a requested amount
023     * reading 0.25 in one log and 0.2500000298 in another, attributed to the pump recomputing
024     * rather than copying the value) is reported in the analysis attached to the linked issue and
025     * is not reproduced by any record committed to this repository.
026     */
027    public static final float INSULIN_FLOAT_EPSILON = 1e-6f;
028
029    protected byte[] cargo = null;
030
031    public HistoryLog() {}
032
033    HistoryLog(long pumpTimeSec, long sequenceNum) {
034        this.pumpTimeSec = pumpTimeSec;
035        this.sequenceNum = sequenceNum;
036    }
037
038    public abstract int typeId();
039
040    long pumpTimeSec = -1;
041    public long getPumpTimeSec() {
042        return pumpTimeSec;
043    }
044
045    public Instant getPumpTimeSecInstant() {
046        return Dates.fromJan12008EpochSecondsToDate(getPumpTimeSec());
047    }
048
049    long sequenceNum = -1;
050    public long getSequenceNum() {
051        return sequenceNum;
052    }
053
054    public abstract void parse(byte[] raw);
055
056    /**
057     * The first two bytes of a history log are a little-endian uint16 whose low 12 bits are the
058     * typeId, leaving these top 4 bits over.
059     *
060     * <p>The 12/4 split is confirmed by Tandem's own Mobi Android app, which reads the first two
061     * bytes little endian and masks with 4095 before looking up the log type
062     * ({@code HistoryLogStreamResponse$HistoryLogStreamCargo}).
063     *
064     * <p><b>What the top 4 bits mean is unknown, and Tandem's app does not appear to care.</b> It
065     * masks them off and discards them: its {@code HistoryLog} model stores the raw bytes, the
066     * masked type, the timestamp, the sequence number and four 4-byte payload fields, with nothing
067     * corresponding to these bits, and nothing in the decompiled app reads them back. The only
068     * records in this repository carrying a nonzero value here are the
069     * {@link DexcomG7CGMHistoryLog} fixtures, which carry 1.
070     *
071     * <p>The value is read and preserved only so that {@code buildCargo} can reproduce such a
072     * record byte for byte. Do not infer a pump model, a firmware version, or a log format from it.
073     *
074     * @return the top 4 bits of the first two cargo bytes, or 0 if the cargo is not populated
075     */
076    public int getHeaderHighNibble() {
077        if (cargo == null || cargo.length < 2) {
078            return 0;
079        }
080        return (Bytes.readShort(cargo, 0) >>> 12) & 0x0F;
081    }
082
083    /**
084     * Builds the leading two cargo bytes from a typeId and the high nibble described in
085     * {@link #getHeaderHighNibble()}. With a nibble of 0 this is identical to the historical
086     * {@code new byte[]{typeId, 0}}, except that it does not truncate a typeId above 255.
087     *
088     * @param typeId the history log typeId, which occupies the low 12 bits
089     * @param headerHighNibble the top 4 bits, of unknown meaning, see {@link #getHeaderHighNibble()}
090     * @return the first two bytes of the cargo, little endian
091     */
092    public static byte[] typeIdBytes(int typeId, int headerHighNibble) {
093        return new byte[]{
094            (byte) (typeId & 0xFF),
095            (byte) (((typeId >> 8) & 0x0F) | ((headerHighNibble & 0x0F) << 4))
096        };
097    }
098
099    /**
100     * Parses the typeId (checked against the superclass static typeId),
101     * pump time in seconds epoch and sequence number.
102     */
103    void parseBase(byte[] raw) {
104        int typeId = Bytes.readShort(raw, 0) & 4095;
105        // skipping due to inconsistencies around signed v unsigned
106        // Validate.isTrue(typeId == typeId(), "found typeId " + typeId + " in message but expected " + typeId());
107
108        this.pumpTimeSec = Bytes.readUint32(raw, 2);
109        this.sequenceNum = Bytes.readUint32(raw, 6);
110    }
111
112    /**
113     * Resets the pumpTimeSec and sequenceNum to 0 so they don't have to be validated in every test clause
114     */
115    void clearBaseFieldsForTesting() {
116        this.pumpTimeSec = 0;
117        this.sequenceNum = 0;
118
119        for (int i=2; i<10; i++) {
120            this.cargo[i] = 0;
121        }
122    }
123
124    public byte[] getCargo() {
125        return this.cargo;
126    }
127
128    public String toString() {
129        return JavaHelpers.autoToString(this, new HashSet<>());
130    }
131
132    public String verboseToString() {
133        return JavaHelpers.autoToStringVerbose(this, Set.of("cargo"));
134    }
135
136    public static byte[] fillCargo(byte[] cargo) {
137        if (cargo.length == 26) {
138            return cargo;
139        }
140        byte[] ret = new byte[26];
141        System.arraycopy(cargo, 0, ret, 0, cargo.length);
142        return ret;
143    }
144
145    public HistoryLogProps props() {
146        return getClass().getAnnotation(HistoryLogProps.class);
147    }
148}
